newsitem.title: USA: Boeing doubles income, but disappoints Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Boeing doubles income, but disappoints Wall Street.

text.p: Boeing Co. said Monday its first-quarter profit more than doubled and its sales grew by 70 percent, reflecting a rise in the number of aircraft delivered, but its results disappointed Wall Street and its shares fell sharply.

Boeing said it earned $313 million, or 87 cents a share, on revenue of $7.32 billion in the period ended March 31. A year earlier, the company earned $119 million, or 35 cents a share, on revenue of $4.29 billion.

The latest earnings of 87 cents a share fell well short of First Call's consensus estimate of $1 a share and Boeing's stock fell sharply on the New York Stock Exchange, opening down $7 at $92 a share.
The stock recovered somewhat at midday, when it traded at $96.25, down $5.75, in very active trading.
"The stock is down because earnings came in quite a bit below the consensus. That's it in a nutshell," said Peter Jacobs, an analyst at Ragan MacKenzie in Seattle.
Boeing said it delivered a total of 68 aircraft during the quarter, up from 40 in the 1996 quarter, when shipments were reduced as a result of a strike in the fourth quarter of 1995.
The world's largest commercial aircraft maker, Boeing said it expected to deliver 90 aircraft during the current quarter.
The company also said it expected the world's airlines to take delivery of $1.1 trillion worth of new aircraft over the next 20 years.

Partially offsetting the increase in Boeing's income were higher research and development expense for the commercial aircraft and defence and space segments, increased interest expense, development expenses related to two joint ventures and a higher income tax rate.
Some of Boeing's increased expenses were related to its acquisition of Rockwell International's defence and aerospace units in December.
Boeing also recorded income of $64 million related to an accounting change at an employee-benefit trust fund in the most recent period.
